reviewer: Codex, personal complete-final-answer read; no paid judge
primary_route: Yeast-juice fractionation, chemical add-back and heat-dependent functional reconstitution.

checks.quote: All experiments below are proposed. The recommended next action is to run a matched reconstitution assay, not to infer chemical identity from the 1906 compensation result. The supplied record supports only an operational hypothesis: a heat-stable factor can be separated from a heat-labile fermentative preparation and is required, together with that preparation, for activity. It does not identify the factor and does not establish NAD identity.
checks.reason: No proposal to consult prior Methods, supplements or validated protocols and verify detailed-condition transfer before execution.
No active-F spike rescue in processed inactive analogs to exclude inhibitors generated during ashing/dialysis.
Buffer identity/concentration and fractionation settings remain unspecified without concrete compatibility/recipe selection.
No product/gas reference recovery/leak/interference accuracy gate and failure action.
No fixed product amount/time convention and full blank/weak-signal treatment, despite explicit failed-tube reporting.
Independent units/nesting correct; n=3 lacks pilot variance/precision/power justification.
Equivalence margin based on noise rather than scientific negligibility; no explicit model/CI/multiplicity procedure for inferential comparisons.
Optional cations plus conductivity do not establish the full ion composition needed for salt exclusion.
No refreeze and fresh independent confirmation after repairs.
Delayed rescue shows some capacity remains, not unchanged enzyme integrity. No standardized excess-complement before/after capacity test separates partial damage/stabilization.
Independent separation helpful, but no operational orthogonal product measurement/specificity/recovery validation.
No raw-file/unit linkage and exact versioned analysis/settings audit.
